blocking_findings: [high][R2-T2-H1] The new fixture breaks the accepted R0 regression contract, contradicting the Green receipt. measure/tracks/business_operations_graph_baseline_remediation_20260730/fixtures/v1/r2-task2-adversarial-fixtures.json was added inside the literal-indexed R0 fixture root but was not added to fixture-index-v1.json. The exact combined command claimed Green at r2-task2-green-receipt-20260731.md:67-68 instead ran 88 tests with one failure: test_literal_fixture_index_pins_every_generated_fixture reports r2-task2-adversarial-fixtures.json as unindexed at measure/tests/test_business_operations_graph_baseline_remediation.py:456-465. This is an accepted-contract regression and an A5 truthfulness violation. Exact remediation: keep the R0 literal trust root unchanged by relocating the R2-only corpus to an R2-owned path, or perform a separately reviewed/versioned R0 contract update; then rerun the exact four-module command and correct the receipt from observed output.

[high][R2-T2-H2] Two-scan provenance is not fail-closed or durable. build_compensation_evidence accepts arbitrary existing graph_db_path and second_scan_db_path values, never executes or verifies the claimed second command, never requires distinct artifacts, and does not bind scan 2's project root or scan-time source state to the materialization it creates. An independent adversary passed graph.db as both arguments; the producer returned scan1EqualsScan2=true, emitted the same SHA for both artifacts, and still labeled scan 2 with the audit-attempt command. The committed test instead hard-codes /tmp/opencode/r2-clean-audit-probe-nbi4_dbp/source/audit-attempt.db at measure/tests/test_business_operations_graph_baseline_r2_compensation.py:47-49, while the evidence retains only its basename/hash/size. That uncommitted temporary database is not replayable in a clean checkout and is not the accepted Task 1 /tmp root recorded in attempt.json. Current bytes happen to match the recorded cbaaa456... hash and all 6,783 archive entries, but current post-hoc equality is not scan-time provenance. This violates FR3.3 and the deterministic/idempotent evidence boundary. Exact remediation: generate scan 2 from a freshly replayed accepted archive in the producer transaction, bracket all 6,783 inputs, retain hash-bound command/config/exit and normalized inventory artifacts durably, reject reused/same artifacts, and make focused tests independent of a machine-local /tmp database.

[high][R2-T2-H3] The omission/tamper corpus is vacuous rather than executable fail-closed coverage. R2Task2AdversarialFixtureTests never opens r2-task2-adversarial-fixtures.json, and no focused test imports or invokes build_compensation_evidence or an evidence validator. The mutation tests only perform tautological assertions such as pop then compare length, replace a digest then assert inequality, or mutate a line number then compare it to the original; they do not require production code to reject the clone. The fixture's duplicate-route case has no corresponding test at all. Consequently every advertised omission/tamper adversary can stay Green even if the producer/consumer accepts the mutation, contrary to fixture non-vacuity and FR3 compensation completeness. Exact remediation: add a strict compensation-evidence validator or producer-input attack seam, parameterize every fixture mutation through it, first prove the valid baseline is accepted and non-empty, require each mutation to raise a specific fail-closed error, and include duplicate route, cross-partition duplicate, anchor/fingerprint/path/name/span tampering, same-scan reuse, and missing ephemeral-artifact cases.
nonblocking_findings: [medium][R2-T2-M1] Whole-file route fallback is correct for the current frozen set but insufficiently constrained for future inputs. Independent graph comparison found exactly 203 null-span routes; every one is a Next page.tsx file and every evidence entry correctly uses lines 1..EOF with the full-file R1 digest, matching the accepted v1 file-based-route convention. However _lookup_positions_for_prefixed_ids applies this fallback to every null-span route without requiring page.tsx or recording fallback provenance, so a null-span route.ts node would be silently represented as an exact RouteHandler declaration. Restrict the fallback to scanner-defined file-based page routes, emit an explicit anchor-provenance field, and add positive page.tsx plus negative non-page null-span tests.
